messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Economic conditions and indicators, Economic policy, public expenditure and revenue, TRADE, INDUSTRY AND MARKETS, and Business/industrial management and organisation in Germany during the 2020s, matching this research need: Longitudinal survey data on German firms during COVID-19, covering executives’ perceptions and expectations, revenues, profits, uncertainty, survival, government support uptake, crisis responses, and planned investment and employment in 2020-2021.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: German firms COVID 2020 2021 longitudinal survey managers expectations revenue profits uncertainty survival government support investment employment dataset
German Business Panel COVID-19 survey firms 2020 2021 data executives expectations profits government aid
action.query: German firms COVID 2020 2021 longitudinal survey managers expectations revenue profits uncertainty survival government support investment employment dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"German Business Panel (GBP) – COVID-19 Survey, 2020–2021","url_or_doi":"https://access.gesis.org/dbk/74082","justification":"Excellent match for the research need. The German Business Panel is a longitudinal survey of German firms that examines the economic consequences of COVID-19 from the perspective of business decision-makers. Its COVID-19 surveys cover 2020–2021, including a second round conducted from November 16, 2020, to June 24, 2021. Variables include executives' perceptions of economic uncertainty, expectations about firm survival, changes in revenue and net income, liquidity, liabilities, government support applications and uptake, managerial crisis responses, and planned investment and employment. The survey also records firm characteristics, industry, organizational practices, and expectations about the broader economy. Particularly relevant for studying how German firms adapted their financial decisions, employment strategies, and investment plans during the pandemic. This is the closest match to the requested combination of topics and variables."},{"title":"IAB Establishments in the COVID-19 Crisis Panel (BeCovid), 2020–2022","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5164/IAB.FDZD.2209.en.v1","justification":"Highly relevant longitudinal establishment survey conducted by Germany's Institute for Employment Research (IAB). The panel includes 24 survey waves collected between August 3, 2020, and June 30, 2022, providing repeated observations of German establishments during the pandemic. It examines the effects of COVID-19 on business operations, employment, workforce adjustments, and organizational responses. Its repeated-wave structure is especially useful for investigating changes in firms' economic circumstances and employment decisions throughout 2020–2021. The linked DOI identifies the official documentation for the longitudinal research data, which are available to external researchers subject to access conditions. It complements the German Business Panel through its detailed establishment-level and labor-market perspective."},{"title":"Bundesbank Online Panel Firms (BOP-F) – German Firm Expectations and Economic Conditions During COVID-19","url_or_doi":"https://www.bundesbank.de/en/tasks/topics/pandemic-weighing-on-many-enterprises-production-and-business-activity-773788","justification":"Strong complementary source for longitudinal research on German executives' economic assessments and expectations during COVID-19. The Deutsche Bundesbank surveyed more than 30,000 German firms across four waves between June 2020 and February 2021, with approximately 10,000 firms participating more than once. The survey covers pandemic-related changes in business activity, economic expectations, financial conditions, and financing difficulties. Its repeated observations permit analysis of changing firm-level perceptions and responses to economic uncertainty. Particularly useful for investigating expectations, financial constraints, and business conditions during the first year of the pandemic. The official Bundesbank page describes the survey and its research applications."},{"title":"ifo Business Survey – Firm-Level Expectations and Responses to the COVID-19 Crisis","url_or_doi":"https://www.ifo.de/en/cesifo/publications/2020/working-paper/firm-level-expectations-and-behavior-response-covid-19-crisis","justification":"Relevant longitudinal survey source for investigating German firms' business expectations and managerial responses to COVID-19. The ifo Institute's representative panel of German firms includes information on business outlooks, expected revenue effects, perceived pandemic impacts, and management decisions. COVID-19-specific questions address expected shutdown duration and crisis responses such as short-time work, reductions in employment, increased working from home, and postponement or cancellation of investments. These variables closely match the requested measures of executives' expectations, uncertainty, crisis management, and planned investment and employment. The linked institutional research page documents the use of the underlying firm-level survey data. Access to individual firm responses may require authorization from the ifo Institute."}]}
